subject: Biotechnology
title: Insulin: Biotech's First Drug
description: Learn Insulin: Biotech's First Drug in one minute.

hook.text: Before 1982, diabetics relied on insulin extracted from pig and cow pancreases — impure and limited.

buildup.text: Genentech inserted the human insulin gene into E. coli bacteria — the cells produced human insulin perfectly.

discovery.text: Humulin became the first FDA-approved recombinant drug in 1982 — biotech proved it could replace animal sourcing.

twist.text: Insulin now costs pennies to produce — yet prices remained high for decades due to patent and market dynamics.

climax.text: Biosimilar insulin finally entered markets — bringing competition that biotech's original promise intended.

punchline.text: Biotech's first drug saved millions — and sparked an industry.

quiz.question: What was the first FDA-approved recombinant DNA drug?
options: Humulin, human insulin produced in E. coli bacteria
Aspirin synthesized by genetically modified yeast

details.summary: In 1982, recombinant human insulin became the first biotechnology drug approved by the FDA. Produced by E. coli bacteria carrying the human insulin gene, it replaced animal-derived insulin and proved that genetic engineering could manufacture life-saving human proteins.
details.whyItMatters: Recombinant insulin was the proof of concept that launched the biopharmaceutical industry. It demonstrated that bacteria could be engineered to produce human proteins at scale, paving the way for hundreds of subsequent biologic drugs.
takeaways: Genentech and Eli Lilly produced the first recombinant human insulin in 1982
E. coli bacteria were engineered with the human insulin gene for production
It replaced animal insulin, reducing allergic reactions and supply limitations

faq.question: Why was recombinant insulin such a breakthrough?
faq.answer: Before 1982, insulin came from pig and cow pancreases, causing allergic reactions in some patients and facing supply limitations. Recombinant human insulin was identical to natural human insulin, eliminated animal sourcing, and proved bacteria could make human medicines.

faq.question: How is recombinant insulin produced in bacteria?
faq.answer: The human insulin gene is inserted into E. coli using a plasmid vector. Bacteria multiply and express the gene, producing insulin protein in large fermentation tanks. The insulin is then purified, folded into its active form, and formulated for injection.
